newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat futures ease in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat futures ease in thin trading.

text.p: Australian wheat futures fell in a thin nervous market on Thursday as drought deepened after Australia's eastern seaboard experienced one of the driest Aprils on record.
Near-term May 1997 traded down by A$5.50 on Tuesday's settlement price to sell at A$190.00, July 1997 fell A$2.50 to A$192.50 while January 1998 fell A$4.00 to A$186.00.
Settlement prices mostly fell by about SA$2.00 a tonne.
The market was nervous over dry weather, Graham Smith of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said.
Some short covering was emerging for May delivery, he said.
Sydney's April was the driest in 101 years, the Bureau of Meteorology said.
The dry has gripped grains areas south of Sydney on Australia's eastern and southeast seaboard, through the states of New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia.
